N1.s: Je %lld gratis Cutlings zijn op. Ga door in Cutling en ontgrendel, dan wordt de nieuwe alsnog bewaard.
N1.back: Your 5 free Cutlings are used-up. Go on in Cutling and unlock, then becomes the new-one still saved.
N1.why: 'Zijn op' is the K1 word for used up; 'Ga door' is the vocabulary's continue button, so the line matches the button iOS shows; 'alsnog' tells them the item they asked for is not lost; 'de nieuwe' because Siri has nothing on screen to point at.

N2.s: Je %lld gratis Cutlings zijn op. Open Cutling en ontgrendel om verder te bewaren.
N2.back: Your 5 free Cutlings are used-up. Open Cutling and unlock to further to save.
N2.why: Same opening as N1 so the limit has one wording; here the app cannot take over, so the person is sent to open it, and 'verder bewaren' echoes S2 'Blijf bewaren'.

N3.why: Capsule in the K1 shape with the middle dot; 'plek' is S6's word for room, 'nog één' with accents says one is left; 29 characters.

N4.why: The used-of-total pair from S29 and M4, so '5 van 5' reads as full without a word that sounds like a warning; 24 characters.

N5.why: The same pair as N4 so the keyboard counts one way; the verbs after the dot are what the tap does, and 'bewaar' tells them this item is still coming; 37 characters.

N6.why: S15's button verb, imperative like every Dutch iOS button; exactly 10 characters.

N7.s: Je %lld gratis Cutlings zijn op. Ontgrendel Cutling, dan wordt deze alsnog bewaard.
N7.back: Your 5 free Cutlings are used-up. Unlock Cutling, then becomes this-one still saved.
N7.why: N1's opening and 'alsnog bewaard'; 'deze' points at the item the form already shows under the notice.

N8.s: Je Cutling staat klaar. Open Cutling en ontgrendel, dan wordt hij bewaard.
N8.back: Your Cutling stands ready. Open Cutling and unlock, then becomes he saved.
N8.why: 'Staat klaar' says the item is held and waiting without using 'bewaard', which is kept for the real save; 'je Cutling' marks the item as theirs so it does not read as the app; 'hij' for a de-word, as Dutch speaks.
